7.6.2. @CHG and File Security
         Section 4 discusses the topic of file security in detail, including references to using
         @CHG to change discretionary access control (DAC) file protection attributes.

         The DAC attributes that can be changed are as follows:

                File privacy state (K, P or Q option)
                Read-only and write-only modes (V, W or Z option)
                Read and write keys (name-1 specified without the K option)

         The following is a summary of the DAC attribute changes available with @CHG:

                Change File Privacy State
                Change Read-Only and Write-Only Modes
                Change Read Key and Write Key
         Change File Privacy State
         The members of the filename-1 F-cycle set changed depend on which of the six
         security software options is configured on the system, whether the file is owned or
         unowned, and which options are specified on @CHG, as follows:

            For systems configured with Fundamental Security, all files are unowned and only
             the P or Q option can be specified to change the file privacy state. The privacy
             change applies to the F-cycle member specified by filename-1. The M option may
             be specified to apply the privacy change to all members of the F-cycle set.
            For systems configured with Security Level 1, 2 or 3, files may be owned or
             unowned. Special security privileges are required to create and maintain unowned
             files.
             -   If the file is owned, then the privacy change applies to all members of the
                 F-cycle set.
             -   If the file is unowned and if the file is currently public or private and if the P or
                 Q option is specified, then the privacy change applies to the F-cycle member
                 specified by filename-1. The M option may be specified to apply the privacy
                 change to all members of the F-cycle set.
             -   If the file is unowned and if either the file is currently ACR-controlled or the K
                 option is specified, then the privacy change applies to all members of the F-
                 cycle set.
            For systems configured with Security Level 3 Controlled Access Protection
             Environment or Security Level 3 Trusted Environment all files are owned and the
             privacy change applies to all members of the F-cycle set.

         Change Read-Only and Write-Only Modes
         Mode changes specified by the V, W, or Z option apply to the F-cycle member
         specified by filename-1. The M option may be specified to apply the changes to all
         members of the F-cycle set.



7830 7949–031                                                                                    7–85
@CHG—Change File or Element Attributes




        Change Read Key and Write Key
        Key changes specified by name-1 apply to all members of the filename-1 F-cycle set.

7.6.3. @CHG Examples for File Changes
        The file changing @CHG examples are presented in the following order:
           Master File Directory Attributes (names, keys, and modes)
           File Caching
           File Security
           Program File Initializing of Program Files
        Master File Directory Attributes (name, keys, and modes)
            @CHG,N FN1.,FN2.

                Changes the file name from FN1 to FN2.
                The qualifier of the file is not changed.
            @CHG FN/KEY1/KEY2.,FN/KEYA.

                The read key of cataloged file FN is changed from KEY1 to KEYA.
                The write key is removed (changed from KEY2 to spaces).
            @CHG,V FN.

                For cataloged file FN, set read-only mode and clear write-only mode.
            @CHG,W FN.

                For cataloged file FN, set write-only mode and clear read-only mode.
            @CHG,ZM FN.

                For all members (M option) of the FN F-cycle set, clear both read-only and
                write-only modes (Z option).

            @CHG,I FN.

                For cataloged file FN, set V-option flag, used along with M option to effect all
                members of FN F-cycle set.

            @CHG,U FN.

                For cataloged file FN, unset (clear) V-option flag, used along with M option to
                effect all members of FN F-cycle set.

        File Caching changes

            @CHG,F FN.,D

                Sets the file-caching specification of file FN to the configured system default.

7.6.4. Changing Program File Element and Version Names
        You can use the @CHG statement to change the element names and version names of
        program file elements. You can also change element names and version names when
        you copy elements with the @COPIN, @COPOUT, and @COPY statements.
        Format
          @CHG[,options] element-name-1,element-name-2[,subtype-list]

        options
           Recognizes the A, C, O, R, S, V, X, and Y options for changing program file element
           and version names.
           You must specify one or more of the A, O, R, and S options. Only the elements of
           types you specify by options have their names changed. You cannot specify
           element cycles.
           When you use the V option for changing an element version, you must also
           include one or more of the A, O, R, and S options. The V option allows the
           changing of element/version names for all elements with the same version name
           as that specified in element-name-1. Only the element types specified by the
           options are changed. You can also use the Y option with the A and V options to
           limit changing element/version names to elements with subtypes that match the
           subtypes specified in the third specification field. See the @COPY statement
           description (see Section 7.14.3) for the definition of the V option, version mask, and
           X option.

        element-name-1
           Specifies the program file element.

        element-name-2
           Specifies the same program file, the new element, and version names.

        subtype-list
           Is a required parameter when the combined AY options are used to restrict
           selected elements to those with subtypes as listed. Each of the executable
           subtypes is defined with a mnemonic.

                       ABS     Absolute
                       OM      Object Module
                       SD      Subsystem Definition
                       ZM      Zero Overhead Object Module
                       BOM     Bound Object Module




7–88                                                                             7830 7949–031
                                                @CHG—Change File or Element Attributes




             Up to three subtypes can be named in a subtype-list. These examples model the
             acceptable options for specifying 1, 2, and 3 subtypes. A maximum of 3 subtypes
             can be specified on a single command.

                1 subtype:    ABS             or ABS.               or ABS//.        or ABS//
                2 subtypes:   ABS/ZM          or ABS/ZM.            or ABS//ZM.
                3 subtypes:   OM/ZM/BOM       or OM/ZM/BOM.

7.6.5. @CHG Examples for Element Changes
         The element changing @CHG examples are presented in the following order:

            Change a specific element or a version name.
            Change a specific element or version using the Y option to restrict subtypes of
             executable elements.
            Change matching elements with a selection criteria governed by use of the V
             option, version masking and variations on name-1 specifications.
            Change matching element names and versions with the X option affecting the
             interpretation of name-2.
         Change a specific element name or version name.

             Specification of the A, O, R, and S options allows you to limit the changes to a
             selected set of element types. Any combination of these four element type
             options can be specified.

             @CHG,OS F1.ELT,F1.NEWELT

                  Change the element name only.

                  The omnibus (O option) and symbolic (S option) elements named ELT in the
                  program file F1 are changed to element name NEWELT.

             @CHG,S F1.ELT1/VER1,F1.ELT2/VER2

                  Change both the element name and version name.

                  The symbolic (S option) element ELT1/VER1 in program file F1 is changed to an
                  element name of ELT2 and a version name of VER2.

             @CHG,A F1.ELT1/VER1,F1.ELT2/VER1

                  Change the element name, but not the version name.

                  The executable (A option) elements named ELT1/VER1 in program file F1 are
                  changed to an element name of ELT2. The version is retained as VER1. This
                  may change more than one element.




7830 7949–031                                                                                   7–89
@CHG—Change File or Element Attributes




               Without the Y option to restrict the change to a list of subtypes, any matching
               executable elements of all subtypes, (Absolute, OM, BOM, ZOOM, and SSD)
               will undergo the requested changes.

           @CHG,R F1.ELT1/VER1,F1.ELT1/VER2

               Change the version name only.

               The version name of relocatable (R option) element ELT1/VER1 in program file
               F1 is changed from VER1 to VER2.

        The Y option

        Change only a select subtype of executable elements.

           To limit the search for matching executable elements (A option) to only certain
           subtypes, add the Y option and provide a subtype-list in specification 3. Presence
           of the Y option requires the A option and it requires a subtype-list in specification
           3.

           @CHG,AY F1.ELT1,F1.ELT2,OM/BOM

               Executable (A option) elements named ELT1 of the OM or ZM subtypes in file
               F1 will be changed to ELT2. Elements named ELT1 of other subtypes (ABS,
               BOM, or SSD) will not be renamed.

        The V option

        Change multiple elements by using version masking or by omitting the element name.

           Using V option allows you to select multiple elements with a common version
           name or with version names containing common specified parts. The V option is
           described in detail in Section 7.14.3.

           Multiple elements can be selected using the V option by:

              Using version masking with the * character.
              Omitting the element name.
              Using version masking AND omitting the element name.
           The selected elements can be of the same element type or of varying element
           types. If any selected elements are of the same element type and are renamed
           with the same element and version name, all but one of the renamed elements
           will be marked as deleted.

           @CHG,SV F1./VER1,F1./VER2

               The input element name is omitted. Therefore, all input element names match.

               The output element name is omitted. Therefore, the input element name is
               carried forward as the output element name.

                                                  @CHG—Change File or Element Attributes




                  All symbolic (S option) elements with any element name and a version name

            @CHG,AV F1.ELT1/V***********,F1.ELT2

7.7. @CKPT and @@CKPT—Save a Complete or
      Partial Copy of a Run
         The @CKPT statement lets you store information about a programming environment
         so that you can halt processing and continue at a later time. The checkpoint/restart
         (CKRS) program consists of two routines: a checkpoint routine and a restart routine.
         Complete information about the CKRS program is in the CKRS Programming
         Reference Manual (7830 7360).

         Format
           @CKPT[,options] [filename.element,,eqpmnt-type,reel-1/.../reel-n,,,,CTL-pool]

         options
            A
                   Does not terminate the run for certain nonfatal errors.
            B
                   Does not save the absolute element being executed. A checkpoint always
                   saves the current state of the program.
            C
                   Indicates checksum of the checkpoint data.
            J
                   Assigns the checkpoint tape as unlabeled.
            M
                   Prints full diagnostic messages without diagnostic snapshots while
                   processing the full checkpoint data.
            N
                   Does not print error messages or diagnostics in the run’s print file.
            P
                   Displays error messages on the console.




7830 7949–031                                                                              7–93
@CKPT and @@CKPT—Save a Complete or Partial Copy of a Run




            Q
                   Prints diagnostic snapshots while processing full checkpoint data. Diagnostic
                   snapshots consist of messages and dumps of specific CKRS data areas at
                   various points in the checkpoint process.
            R
                   Saves the mass storage symbiont files. (Tape symbiont files are always
                   saved.)
            S
                   Performs only a partial checkpoint.

            T
                   Terminates the current batch run if the checkpoint is successfully taken.
                   For demand runs, only the program terminates.
            Z
                   Prints diagnostic snapshots while processing partial checkpoint data.

        filename
            Identifies the file for the checkpoint. The file name is optional if you specify the
            reel number and the J option. A file name not followed by a period is treated as an
            element in TPF$ if you specify a version or element cycle or both, if this is a partial
            checkpoint. A file name not followed by a period is treated as a file name if this is
            a full checkpoint. A file name can include the directory-ID.

        element
            Identifies the element for the checkpoint. This element cannot reside in a Large
            Element Program File (LEPF).
            If you specify an element, CKRS writes the checkpoint information to that
            element.
            If you do not specify an element and the file is not a tape file, the checkpoint is
            written from the beginning of the file. More details and examples are given in the
            CKRS Programming Reference Manual (7830 7360).

        eqpmnt-type
            This optional field identifies the equipment type if you are using a tape and if
            filename is neither cataloged nor assigned.

        reel-n
            Specifies the reel number of the tape the checkpoint is written to. This is optional.
            You cannot specify expiration-period, ring-indicator, and ACR-name, but you must
            include the commas for these fields if you use the CTL-pool field.

         CTL-pool
            Can be one of the following:
            CTL-pool-name
                   Directs the Exec to allocate a BLANK cartridge from the designated Cartridge
                   Tape Library (CTL) pool of cartridge tapes.

            NONCTL
                   Directs the Exec to use freestanding cartridge tape drives.

         Examples
            Examples of @CKPT are given in the CKRS Programming Reference Manual (7830

7.8. @CLOSE—Close Tape File
         The @CLOSE statement closes the specified magnetic tape files by writing two
         hardware EOFs on the associated magnetic tape and rewinding it. The @CLOSE
         statement performs the same operations as the @MARK statement followed by the
         @REWIND statement.

         Only the filename-1 parameter is required in the @CLOSE statement.

         Format
           @CLOSE[,options] filename-1 [,filename-2,...,filename-n ]

         options
            C
                   Do not take ERR$ exit if an error is detected.

                   Use of the C option on any FURPUR command will prevent execution of ER
                   ERR$ on error exit if FURPUR is running in breakpoint or batch. The C option
                   should be used with caution because a bad result of an erroring FURPUR
                   command could be input to a process later on in the runstream.

                   The C option is valid for all FURPUR commands.

            I
                   Rewind with interlock. If the I option is omitted, the tape is rewound without
                   interlock.

         filename-n
            Specifies the tape files to be closed.




7830 7949–031                                                                                7–95
@@CM—Send a Message to the Operator Console




7.9. @@CM—Send a Message to the Operator
      Console
       The @@CM statement is another way you can send a message to the operator
       console.

       One of the main differences between the @MSG statement and this statement is that
       the @MSG statement must be used within an active run, whereas the @@CM
       statement can be used outside of a runstream (before an @RUN statement or after an
       @FIN statement). In addition, the @@CM message is prefixed by your site-ID instead of
       your user-ID. You can think of the @@CM statement as a console message statement.

       Format
         @@CM message

       message is the message you are sending and can be up to 57 characters long.

       Example
         @@CM PLEASE CHECK IF TAPE 3556A IS THERE

       Sends the message following @@CM to the operator console.


7.10. @@CONS—Enter Console Keyins
       The @@CONS statement allows you to enter console keyins This subsection shows
       you two ways to enter console keyins. It also supplies a table of console mode keyins
       that can be used and the console mode required for each keyin (Table 7-2).

       Format 1
       Use this format when you want to enter a series of unsolicited keyins:
         @@CONS
         keyin 1
         keyin 2
          .
          .
          .
         keyin n
         @@END CONS

       The @@END CONS statement terminates console mode. If you do not enter an
       @@END CONS statement, you stay in console mode until you type in an @@TERM or
       @FIN statement.

       If you have display-and-keyin mode or response-and-keyin mode, you can use option
       letter K on the N @@CONS statement to inhibit automatic displaying of message
       groups, as follows:
         @@CONS,K




7–96                                                                            7830 7949–031
                                                              @@CONS—Enter Console Keyins




         Format 2
         Use this format when you want to enter only one keyin:
             @@CONS[,host-id] keyin

         host-ID
              Can be A through L. The host-ID is valid only if your system has Multi-Host File
              Sharing. Using this option lets you submit a keyin on one host for processing on
              another host in the file-sharing environment. The response is routed back to the
              original host. The output display does not indicate the host-ID of the processing
              host.

         keyin
              Includes the keyin and the text of the keyin.

         Note: If you enter @@CONS keyin between an @@CONS and an @@END CONS
         statement (see Format 1), and you do not include any other keyins between those
         statements, the @@CONS and @@END CONS are extraneous (unless a
         read-and-reply message is possible as a result of the keyin).

7.10.1. Operating Considerations
         The following operating considerations apply to the @@CONS statement:

             As with all previous Exec levels, the start-of-entry (SOE) solicitation of input at a
              demand terminal (or through the ER RSI$ interface) is unpredictable after a user
              enters the @@CONS statement. That is, solicitation cannot occur.
              See the ER Programming Reference Manual (7830 7899) for more information on
              ER RSI$.

             Read-only console messages and the message groups display can be discarded
              when they build up. You receive a warning message when console output is lost.
              When you terminate console mode, passing of message groups and read-and-
              reply messages to your terminal ends. The output (normal output from a keyin
              routine) is displayed until the keyin routine sends the last line of output.

             For Asian messages sent to remote consoles (@@CONS)
                  The Exec Console Message Handler does not check a remote console to
                   make sure that it can translate and display 2-byte Asian characters. If the
                   console cannot, what is displayed is uncertain.
                  A 2-byte Asian character can be truncated in the middle of the 2 bytes,
                   causing that character to be displayed incorrectly. (The Exec Console
                   Message Handler does not check for this.)




7830 7949–031                                                                                    7–97
@@CONS—Enter Console Keyins




7.10.2. Console Modes
          As a demand terminal operator, you can perform many of the console commands
          used by a system console operator. Console commands, sometimes called keyins, are
          instructions that tell the Exec to perform certain tasks. The console commands you
          are allowed to use are determined by the remote console mode capability level given
          to you by your site administrator. There are five levels of console mode capabilities:

             Basic

             Limited

             Full

             Display

             Response

          Following are descriptions of each console mode. Each console mode is described in
          terms of the maximum console command capabilities possible for that console mode
          level. Whether you actually have the maximum, or a subset of the maximum, console
          commands allowed in a particular mode depends on how the site administrator sets
          up your user-ID. For example, a limited mode user might be restricted to doing only
          the symbiont console commands. See the ClearPath OS 2200 Apex Help (8207 4154)
          or the SIMAN Administration and End Use Guide (TQ-01151) for more information on
          how your site administrator configures your user-ID for console commands.

Basic
          This mode lets you manipulate or request information on your run, on any run started
          by you, or on any run controlled by your user-ID.

Limited
          In this mode, you can use all the commands specified in basic mode, and you can use
          many of the status commands.

Full
          With full console capability, you can use most of the unsolicited commands. However,
          you are not allowed to use the security, performance analysis, and common bank
          reload keyins, and a few others.




7–98                                                                             7830 7949–031
                                                           @@CONS—Enter Console Keyins




Display
          This mode lets you use the same console commands as in full mode and also displays
          message groups at your terminal. You can see all message groups or a subset of the
          message groups defined at your site, depending on how your user-ID is configured.
          For more information on message groups, see the Exec Operations Reference
          Manual (7831 0281).

          Display console mode gives you capabilities similar to those of an onsite system
          console operator, with the following exceptions:

             Your terminal cannot be a boot console.
             Your terminal cannot be a response console for a group. In other words, you
              cannot reply to read-and-reply messages. The system operator cannot use an AC
              keyin to make your terminal a response console.
             The system status continuous display is not sent to your terminal.
             No special scrolling procedures are used for messages coming to your terminal.

Response
          This mode lets you use all unsolicited commands except COLOR and AC. This mode
          also lets your terminal act as a display or response console, or both, for the message
          groups configured for your user-ID. This mode has all the privileges and limits of
          display mode, with the following exceptions:

             Your terminal can be the response console for one or more specified message
              groups. Up to 10 read-and-reply messages can be displayed at the same time;
              their message numbers range from 0 to 9. The message number is not removed
              from the message once the message is answered.

             You can issue console commands without having answered any outstanding read-
              and-reply messages.

             If no command groups are selected for your user-ID, you can perform all the
              keyins except AC. If specific command groups are selected, you can perform only
              the commands in those groups and the MR command.
          Refer to the Exec Operations Reference Manual (7831 0281) for the actual console
          command descriptions and other operator procedures.

          The dynamic configuration parameter, echo_remote_console, can be used to specify
          that messages for the system console must be displayed on the local system console
          in addition to any active remote response console.




7830 7949–031                                                                                7–99
@@CONS—Enter Console Keyins




7.10.3. Console Mode Input/Output Rules
        Following are various rules associated with using console modes.

Terminating Console Mode
        Entering an @@END CONS statement terminates console mode. Once you have
        terminated console mode, any input you enter is treated as regular input. This includes
        unsolicited commands and responses to read-and-reply messages resulting from the
        processing of unsolicited commands.

        When you are not in console mode and you type in an @@CONS command statement,
        console mode is terminated immediately after the command has been accepted. If this
        statement contains a command that results in a read-and-reply (such as a DN
        command), the read-and-reply is not displayed at the terminal and you cannot respond
        to the read-and-reply.

        If a read-only message is outstanding or occurs after you have terminated console
        mode, the message is discarded.

Message Group Display Termination
        Termination of display mode or response mode also terminates all message groups
        going to your terminal. If you initiate display mode or response mode with an
        @@CONS command statement, no message groups are displayed because console
        mode is terminated before routing of the message groups is set up.

Read-and-Reply Messages
        Read-and-reply messages and responses to these messages are handled in the
        following ways:

           If a read-and-reply message is outstanding or occurs after you have terminated
            console mode, the message, along with a header message if the read-and-reply
            message was the result of a previous unsolicited command, is sent to an onsite
            console. The format of the header is as follows:
              RESULT OF KEYIN FROM site-id

            If you have response mode, no header is sent if the read-and-reply message was
            not the result of a previous unsolicited command.
            If you do not have response mode, once a read-and-reply message has been
            displayed at your terminal, no additional input other than a response to that
            message is allowed. If you enter other input, the following message appears:
              *ANSWER MESSAGE*




7–100                                                                           7830 7949–031
                                                             @@CONS—Enter Console Keyins




             A redisplay of the read-and-reply message appears next. The following cycle
             continues until you answer the message, the terminal times out, you leave
             console mode, or you type in @@TERM:
             1.    The system accepts your input.
             2.    It verifies the input as a response.
             3. It sends the reject message and the original read-and-reply message if the
                answer is unacceptable.

             If the input is acceptable, it is sent to the routine that issued the read-and-reply
             message, and the console handler deletes the original read-and-reply message.
             The routine then determines whether the response is correct and reissues the
             message if it is not.
             The read-and-reply message sent to a terminal has the following format:
                  # read-and-reply-message

             where # is the read-and-reply message number.

             The answer (also called a solicited keyin) to the read-and-reply message must be
             in this format:
                  # answer

            If you have response mode, some read-and-reply messages associated with a
             particular message group can already be displayed on a local console. These
             messages are not redisplayed at your remote console; they must be answered at
             the local console.

Print Output
         If you have limited console mode, you cannot terminate print files (using the SX keyin)
         from runs other than your own. If you have full, display, or
         response mode, and you are allowed to enter the symbiont group of console
         commands, you can terminate any print files.

         Note: The Exec and communications software do not attempt to segregate print
         output from console output (while in console mode); or console output from print
         output (once console mode has terminated).

7.11. @@CONT—Continue to Send Output
        The @@CONT statement tells the system to resume sending output to the terminal
        after you have interrupted it with the MSG WAIT key. (Although you can continue
        output by just pressing the XMIT key, it can generate an error message, or the blank
        line might be accepted by the executing program.)

        Format
             @@CONT


7.12. @COPIN—Copy from Tape to Program Files
        The @COPIN statement copies one or more elements from an element file located on
        magnetic tape into a program file located on sector-formatted mass storage. Large
        Element Program Files (LEPFs and LLEPFs) cannot be used as output program files for
        COPIN.

        When a relocatable element is added to a program file, any entry-point table that can
        have existed for the file before the execution of the @COPIN relocatable statement is
        destroyed. You can use the @PREP statement (see Section 7.46) to recreate the
        relocatable entry-point table. If a tape error occurs, only those elements completely
        transferred before the error occurred are entered in the program file and listed in its
        table of contents.

        Format
             @COPIN[,options] name-1,name-2

        options
              Can be file options or element options (listed in the following "File Options" and
              "Element Options").


7–108                                                                               7830 7949–031
                                           @COPIN—Copy from Tape to Program Files




            File Options
            Following are the @COPIN statement options which are specified when name-1 is
            a file name:
            None
                Used to copy elements from the input magnetic tape file (in element file
                format) into the program file located on sector-formatted mass storage. The
                tape file must be positioned at the label block of the first element being
                copied (use the @FIND statement, see Section 7.29) and continues until a
                hardware EOF mark is encountered. The elements retain the element names
                used in the element file.

            A,O,R,S
                Same operation as if no options were specified, except that the A, O, R, and
                S options can be used to designate the type of element to be copied. Any
                combination of A, O, R, and S can be used. All elements of the types
                specified are transferred. The elements retain the names they had in the
                element file.

            C
                Used to direct FURPUR not to exit through ERR$ if an error is encountered.

                Use of the C option on any FURPUR command will prevent execution of ER
                ERR$ on error exit if FURPUR is running in breakpoint or batch. The C option
                should be used with caution because a bad result of an erroring FURPUR
                command could be input to a process later on in the runstream.

                The C option is valid for all FURPUR commands.

            V
                Same as for elements.

            X
                Same as for elements.

            Element Options
            Following are the @COPIN statement options which are specified when name-1 is
            an element name:
            A,O,R,S
                Used to copy one element and insert it into the output program file. The
                element name remains the same unless renamed in name-2.

            V
                Used to copy elements having the same version name from an element file
                on magnetic tape into a program file on sector-formatted mass storage. The
                input file must be positioned at the label block of the first element to be
                copied. Copying continues until a hardware EOF mark is encountered. See



7830 7949–031                                                                          7–109
@COPIN—Copy from Tape to Program Files




                  the @COPY statement description in Section 7.14.3 for a definition of the V
                  option and version mask.

           X
                  Used to exchange name-2 form interpretation for V option processing. See
                  the @COPY statement description in Section 7.14.3.

        name-1
           Specifies the input tape file or input element to be copied.

        name-2
           Specifies the output program file or output program file and element name. If
           name-1 is an element name and name-2 is a file name, the element retains its
           name in the new file.

        Examples
        The following examples illustrate the use of the @COPIN statement:
          @COPIN HOLDPROG.,PROGRAM.

                 The element file located on magnetic tape file HOLDPROG is copied into
                 program file PROGRAM on sector-formatted mass storage.

          @COPIN,R TEMP.ELTA,PF1.

                 Relocatable element ELTA in element file on tape file TEMP is copied into
                 program file PF1. The relocatable entry-point table of file PF1 is destroyed (an
                 @PREP statement is needed to rebuild the relocatable entry-point table; see
                 Section 7.47).

          @COPIN,RV A./B,C.

                 All relocatable elements in element file on tape file A with the version name B
                 are copied into program file C. They retain the version name B in the program
                 file.

          @COPIN,SV A.,C.

               All symbolic elements in element file on tape file A with a blank version name
               are copied into program file C. These elements added to the program file retain
               blank version names.

          @COPIN,R PET.ELT3,REPET.VERSG

               The relocatable element in element file on tape file PET with the element name
               ELT3 and a blank version name is copied into program file REPET and given the
               element name VERSG with a blank version name.




7–110                                                                              7830 7949–031
                                                   @COPOUT—Copy Program Files to Tape




           @COPIN,O T.,F.

                All omnibus elements in element file on tape file T are copied into program file F.
                The element and version names remain the same.

           @COPIN,SV TAPE./V***********,FAST.

                All symbolic elements in element file on tape file TAPE having a version name
                beginning with V are copied into program file FAST. The element and version
                names remain the same.

           @COPIN,AV TAP.OLDABS/VERS********,FAS.

                All executable elements named OLDABS having a version name beginning with
                VERS are copied into program file FAS. The element and version names remain
                the same. See the description of the @COPY statement (Section 7.14.3) for
                examples of how to use the X option.


7.13. @COPOUT—Copy Program Files to Tape
         The @COPOUT statement copies a program file or selected elements from a program
         file located on sector-formatted mass storage into a magnetic tape file in element file
         format. Large Element Program Files (LEPF and LLEPFs) cannot be used as input
         program files for COPOUT.

         Procedure name entries are saved but relocatable entry points are discarded. Tape
         files must be in element file format in order to use the @COPIN and @FIND statements
         (see Sections 7.12 and 7.29).

         Note: If you just want to save a program file on tape, it is faster and more
         efficient to use the @COPY,G statement instead of the @COPOUT statement.

         All parameters of the @COPOUT statement are optional except name-2.

         Format
           @COPOUT[,options] [name-1], name-2

         options
             The choices are either file or element options.

             File Options
             The following are the @COPOUT statement options that can be specified when
             name-1 is a file name:
             None
                   Used to write all nondeleted elements onto the magnetic tape output file in
                   element file format. For unlabeled tapes, two EOF marks are written at the
                   end of the file and the tape is backspaced one EOF mark. For labeled tapes,
                   one EOF mark is written and the tape is positioned after the EOF mark.
                   Elements retain the element name they had in the program file.


7830 7949–031                                                                                 7–111
@COPOUT—Copy Program Files to Tape




          A, O, R, S
               Used to write all nondeleted elements of the types specified by the options
               onto the magnetic tape output file in element file format. The elements retain
               the names they had in the program file. Any combination of A, O, R, and S can
               be used. No EOF mark is written.

          C
               Used to direct FURPUR not to exit through ERR$ if an error is encountered.

               Use of the C option on any FURPUR command will prevent execution of ER
               ERR$ on error exit if FURPUR is running in breakpoint or batch. The C option
               should be used with caution because a bad result of an erroring FURPUR
               command could be input to a process later on in the runstream.

               The C option is valid for all FURPUR commands.

          E
               Used for unlabeled tapes to improve write performance. At the end of the
               file, write a single EOF mark instead of writing two EOF marks and
               backspacing over one of them. Before finishing with the tape (for example
               @FREE, @MOVE,B or @REWIND), you must close the output tape with
               @CLOSE (see Section 7.8) or @MARK (see Section 7.38). The E option cannot
               be used with the A, O, R, S, V, or X options, which do not write an EOF mark.
               The E option is ignored for labeled tapes, which always write a single EOF
               mark.

          V
               Same as for elements.

          W
               Used when the buffered-write mode BUFTAP is enabled on the output tape
               to assure that all buffered data has successfully been written to tape. After
               the write of the EOF mark, a synchronize (FSAFE$) I/O function is issued, if
               necessary. Note that the synchronize increases the time to write this file, as
               if the buffered-write mode BUFFIL was enabled. To maximize performance
               the W option must be used only periodically, to establish error recovery
               "checkpoints." The W option cannot be used with the A, O, R, S, V, or X
               options, which do not write an EOF mark. The W option is ignored for
               unlabeled tapes when the E option is not specified. In the latter two cases,
               the tape is implicitly synchronized by the Exec or by the tape unit.

          X
               Same as for elements.

            Element Options
            The following are the @COPOUT statement options that can be specified when
            name-1 is an element name:
            A, O, R, S
                    Used to write all specified element types for the element names given into
                    the output magnetic tape file in element file format. Only nondeleted
                    elements are transferred. If the name-1 and name-2 element names are
                    different, all elements copied have the name-2 element name. One or more
                    options must be specified. No EOF mark is written.

            V
                    Used to write all nondeleted elements, selected by version name and type,
                    onto the magnetic tape output file in element file format. The V option can be
                    used in combination with the A, O, R, and S options. When it is used alone, all
                    element types are considered. See the description of the @COPY statement
                    in 7.14.3 for a definition of the V option and version mask.

         @MARK statement (see Section 7.38).

         name-1
                Specifies the input program file or element to be copied. If you do not specify
                name-1, the default (TPF$) is used.

         name-2

         The following examples illustrate the use of the @COPOUT statement:

           @COPOUT PROGRAM.,HOLDPROG.

            options are specified, a hardware EOF mark is written following the output file.

             specified.

            @COPOUT,R A.,B.

             unchanged.

7.14. @COPY—Copy Files or Elements
        The @COPY statement copies between SDF files, program files, and program file
        elements. The @COPY functions can be divided into these categories:

        File to File (see Section 7.14.1)

            SDF files into a destination SDF file
            All program file elements into a destination program file
            Program file elements of selected types into a destination program file

             A single program file element into a destination program file element
             SDF file contents into a program file element
             A program file element into an SDF file
             Sets of program file elements into a destination program file
         The format of the basic @COPY statement is the same for either of the category.

         All parameters of the @COPY statement are optional.

         Format
             @COPY[,options] [name-1,name-2,{ number-of-files | subtype-list } ]

         options
              The options possible depend on which type of COPY is requested.

         name-1

         name-2

              When used, it indicates the number of files to copy; if omitted, 1 is assumed.
              When used for tape-to-tape copying of entire files, it specifies the number of input
              files to copy onto the output tape. The input tape remains positioned between the
              two EOF marks. The number of blocks in each file copied and the number of files
              copied are indicated in the output listing.
              When used in conjunction with the B option, it specifies the number of OS 2200
              FORTRAN files to copy from one file to another. The number of files copied is
              indicated in the output listing.
              When an attempt is made to copy an empty file (two hardware EOFs), the copy
              operation is immediately terminated regardless of the contents of the
              number-of-files parameter.

         subtype-list
              In addition to specifying the number of files, you can also use the third
              specification to specify the mnemonics of executable element subtypes.

7.14.1. File-based Copy Options
        Mass storage files can be either word-addressable or sector-formatted. When copying
        from one mass storage to another, any combination is allowed (sector to word, word
        to word, word to sector, or sector to sector).

        The following are the options that you can supply for @COPY statements to copy a
        source file into a destination file:

        None
               Copying from mass storage to mass storage–Used to overwrite one mass
                storage file (name-2) with the contents of another mass storage file (name-1),
                without regard to the file format and size. If name-2 is smaller than name-1,
                copying is done partially (till end of name-2).
               Copying from tape-to-tape–Used to copy one or more files (depending on
                number-of-files parameter) from the input tape to the output tape without
                regard to the file format. No hardware EOF marks are written. Block size is
                limited to 65,000 words.
               Copying from mass storage to tape–Used to copy the contents of a mass
                storage file to an output tape. The mass storage file is copied to tape a track
                at a time with blocks written to tape to represent any unassigned (whole)
                tracks in the mass storage file. At the conclusion of the copy, no EOF is
                written to the tape. This allows appending of additional files to the tape.
                @MARK must be used to place an EOF at the end of the file. This is a very
                simple, unformatted copy and in most cases another copy command (COPY,G)
                would probably be much more useful for depositing single mass storage file
                contents to tape.

                number of the track, beginning with zero. Only allocated mass storage tracks
                up to and including the highest track written are read. The physical tape block
                size is fixed for each file and is a multiple of 1,794 words, as described for the

7.14.2. Element-based Copy Options
         The following are the options that you can supply to @COPY statements that copy

            A source element into a destination element
            A source element into a destination file
            A source file into a destination element
         A, O, R, S
             Used to restrict the copy of the specified element from the input file to those
             matching the type specified. Any combination of A, O, R, and S can be used. Any
             existing elements that are duplicated as a result of the copy are deleted in the
             destination file. If the element being deleted is a PROC element, all associated
             PROC names in the procedure table are deleted.
             The options represent the types of elements to be copied (one or more are
             needed). The element name can be changed by renaming it in name-2. Both input
             and output files must be on sector-formatted mass storage. When a symbolic
             element is being copied, all element cycles are copied unless an element cycle is
             specified in name-1 or if the L option is specified on the call (in which case, the
             output element produced is designated as cycle zero).
             Element cycles cannot be specified in name-1 for Assembler, FORTRAN, or
             COBOL procedure elements. Element cycles cannot be specified in name-2.

         I
             Used to copy an SDF file to a program file as a new symbolic element or to copy a
             symbolic element into an SDF file. The SDF file can be either a tape file or a sector-
             formatted mass storage file.
                SDF to Element

                 The SDF file is copied into a new symbolic type element in the destination
                 program file. If the O option is also present, the new element will be created
                 as an omnibus type.
                 Reading of the input file is terminated by an SDF EOF control record.
                 The new element retains the SDF records of the file from which it was
                 created. When the new element is referenced, S3, S4, S5, S6 in the control
                 records can be treated as cycle information by many system processors.
                Element to SDF

                 A symbolic-type element is copied into a new SDF file. If the O option is also
                 present, the new file will be created from a source element of the omnibus
                 type.
                 All deleted images from the source element are removed.
                 If the source element is in SIR$ format, all element cycle information in the
                 image control words is zeroed. Otherwise, the copy is done in blocks with no
                 checking of image control words.




7830 7949–031                                                                                7–123
@COPY—Copy Files or Elements




Element-based Copy Options (continued)
        L
            Used with the S option to copy the latest cycle of the element in name-1. The
            output element is designated as cycle zero. The L option is ignored if the element
            in name-1 is an Assembler, FORTRAN, or COBOL procedure element, or if the
            element in name-1 is not general symbolic type SDF.

        O
            Usable only in conjunction with the I option. When present, it indicates use of
            omnibus elements, rather than symbolic elements, in copies between SDF files
            and Program File elements.
            When copying from a file to an element, the mass storage file cannot contain any
            unallocated areas (holes).
        V
            Allows you to broaden your selection of elements by using version masking (the
            asterisk character) or by omission of either the element or the version name from
            the name-1 specification. For details, see Section 7.14.3.

        Y
            Can only be used in conjunction with the A option. The AY options restrict the
            copy of executable type elements to the subtypes indicated in the subtype-list in
            specification 3.

        X
            For output element specifications (name-2), the X option affects the interpretation
            of an omitted version name. The previous version name can be retained or
            removed (replaced by blanks). See Section 7.14.3 for a detailed description.

        When a procedure element is copied, the procedure name entries are automatically
        added to the procedure name table of the output file.

        If a relocatable element is copied, the relocatable entry-point table of the output file is
        destroyed and the @PREP statement (see Section 7.46) must be used to recreate it.

        Before you do any copy operation from tape, you might need to execute an @MOVE
        statement (see Section 7.40) to position the tape beyond some EOF mark. No @COPY
        operation moves backward or forward over an EOF mark before the start of the copy.

7.14.3. Version Masking, Multiple Element Selection, and the V
        and X Options
         There are times when you want to select multiple elements to copy instead of a
         single individual element. You may want to copy all elements with a particular element
         or version name. Perhaps you may want to copy all elements with version names
         starting with the letter A. To allow multiple element selection, FURPUR provides these
         methods to select a multiple element set on a single FURPUR statement.

         The following methods can be used together or separately. These selection methods
         are activated by using the V option on FURPUR statements that accept an input
         element specification. Each of these methods is described in detail in the following
         sections.

         1.   Omission of name-1 (input) specification for element name or version name.
         2.   Using version masking in the version part of name-1 (input) specification.
         3. Omission of name-2 (output) specification for element name or version name
            along with use of the X option.
         The V option can be used on element-based formats of the following FURPUR
         statements. File-based formats of these statements have a different meaning, or no
         meaning, ascribed to the V option.

                @CHG,V         input-elt-spec, output-elt-spec
                @COPIN,V       tape-name, output-elt-spec
                @COPOUT,V      input-elt-spec, tape-name
                @COPY,V        input-elt-spec, output-elt-spec
                @DELETE,V      input-elt-spec
                @PRT,TV        input-elt-spec

         The V option can be used in conjunction with any of the element type options (A, O, R,
         or S). If no element type options are specified to limit the scope of selection, the
         assumption is that all types are selectable.

         The ability to select multiple elements for any of the supported statements is a
         powerful tool which should be used judiciously. Using the V option allows a repeated
         action on multiple input elements that may result in unintended deletion of existing
         elements. For example:

             Renaming multiple input elements to have the same output element and version
              name.
             Creating a new element into a program file where that element name and version
              already exists.
         In such cases, any existing elements are marked as deleted when new elements with
         the same element name, version name, and in the case of executable elements, same
         subtype, are added through renaming of an existing element (@CHG) or creating a new
         element (@COPY).

7.14.4. @COPY Examples
        The following examples illustrate the use of the @COPY statement. The examples are
        presented in alphabetical order.
          @COPY,AOV FI./VERS,FO.

           version name of VERS are copied into program file FO. Element and version names
           remain unchanged.

          @COPY,ARSV FILE1./V***********,FILE2.

           All nondeleted executable, relocatable, and symbolic elements in program file
           FILE1 that have a version name beginning with V are copied into program file FILE2
           with element and version names unchanged.

          @COPY,AY F11.ELT1,F86.ELT2,OM

           If the element is an executable type and has a subtype of OM, FURPUR copies the
           element ELT1 from the file F11 to the file F86 and changes its name to ELT2.
           executable type and has a subtype of OM.

            @COPIN statements cannot be used to access the file; however, the @COPY,G
            format makes more economical use of time and space. When you return the file
            (@COPY,G) to sector-formatted mass storage, the file is reproduced as it was
            before, including all tables of contents and deleted elements. Do not attempt to
            merge two program files, each of which were saved on tape using the @COPY,GM
